markdown:
# Icon

You might say
Add a small icon to the button so people can tell what it does without reading.

**A small, consistent visual symbol for an action, object, or status**·Familiar icons such as search, download, and close help people scan quickly. For an unfamiliar or high-risk action, add text or a [Tooltip](/vibe-hub/tooltip?lang=en).

## You can say this to an AI Agent

> “
> Review the project toolbar: familiar actions may use consistent icons, but permanent deletion must also show explicit text and use a real button. Do not rely only on red or a tooltip, and verify keyboard access and the accessible name.

Icon**≠**[Image](/vibe-hub/image?lang=en)

[Icon](/vibe-hub/icon?lang=en) is a small reusable symbol for a function or concept. [Image](/vibe-hub/image?lang=en) displays a photo, illustration, or content itself.

Icon**≠**[Button](/vibe-hub/button?lang=en)

[Icon](/vibe-hub/icon?lang=en) communicates meaning. It becomes an icon button only when placed in a [Button](/vibe-hub/button?lang=en) that runs an action.

### When to use it

- Common tool actions

⌕↓×Search · Download · Close
- Compact toolbars

↶↷⌗⋯
- Status cues with text

✓File synced

### When NOT to use it

- An unfamiliar action with only an icon

◈The icon’s meaning is unclear
- Unrelated dangerous actions mixed under More

⋯Delete project is hidden under More
- Emoji in place of consistent system icons

⬇📥⇩Three download icons with inconsistent styles
